title: A Pilot Towards Embedded Evaluations
summary: A Pilot Towards Embedded Evaluations Announcing a pilot towards embedded evaluations with OpenAI CEO Marius Hobbhahn speaks on misaligned AI in the U.S. Senate Who We Are About Team Press Blog Science Monitoring Governance Careers Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher · Try Watcher All blog posts A Pilot Towards Embedded Evaluations Written & Edited By Apollo Research Team Published on 16 November 2026 Table of Contents Evaluating anti-scheming training Share this post Copy as Markdown Apollo Research is excited to announce a pilot towards embedded evaluations with OpenAI. As part of this pilot, a team of six from Apollo Research will work within OpenAI for four months, assessing the alignment of models throughout training, evaluations, and internal deployment with scoped rules of access. Apollo Research’s goal is to investigate whether models attempt to subvert their own or their successors’ alignment or control mechanisms . This pilot will focus on examining four areas across development: Whether training incentivizes subversion Whether evaluations can elicit subversion Whether subversion occurs during internal deployment Whether reasoning relevant to subversion would be detectable. summary: red.anthropic.com red .anthropic.com Articles June 2026 Measuring LLMs' Impact on N-day Exploits In cybersecurity, a large fraction of real-world harm comes from N-days: vulnerabilities that have already been publicly disclosed, but only patched on some devices. In this post, we evaluate how much large language models can accelerate and automate the process of developing N-day exploits. Mapping AI-enabled cyber threats: Insights from the LLM ATT&CK Navigator We’ve spent the past year investigating how threat actors are weaponizing AI to conduct cyber operations. Today, we’re sharing a new analysis that maps these real-world attacks onto the MITRE ATT&CK framework, a database of tactics and techniques used by cyberattackers. We partnered with Verizon to include some of these results in the 2026 Verizon Data Breach Investigation Report (DBIR), and are publishing this report to offer a longer-form analysis of trends we are seeing in AI-enabled cyber operations.
